tip: Que before an adjective or noun makes an exclamation meaning how or what a. Que legal = how cool.
Massa literally means dough or mass, but as slang it means awesome or cool. Que massa = that's awesome.
Livre comes from livrar (to free), so Deus me livre literally asks God to spare you from something bad.
Mesmo after a word adds emphasis, like really or for real. Sério mesmo means are you seriously for real.
Nessa is em + essa (in or on that one). Vamos nessa literally is let's go on this one, meaning let's do it.
Achar literally means to find, but in acho que it means to think or reckon. Eu acho que sim = I think so.
Nem means not even. Nem pensar is literally not even to think about it, a firm way to say no way.
Por + o contracts to pelo, so you congratulate with parabéns pelo. Parabéns pelo trabalho = congrats on the work.
For feelings and states, use estar com plus a noun. Tô com preguiça is literally I'm with laziness, meaning I feel lazy.
Esquentar a cabeça literally is to heat the head and means to worry. Não esquenta a cabeça = don't stress about it.
Tô ligado literally means I'm switched on, and as slang it means I'm aware or I got it. Tô ligado = understood.
Gente usually means people, but gente boa describes one kind, decent person. Você é gente boa = you're a good person.
Estar de saco cheio is a mildly crude idiom for being fed up. Tô de saco cheio disso = I'm sick of this.
Trouxe is the irregular past of trazer (to bring), not a regular ending. Ele trouxe comida = he brought food.
Fazer uma pergunta pairs fazer (to make) with pergunta to mean ask a question. Posso te fazer uma pergunta = can I ask you a question.
Estar de olho em means to keep an eye on someone. Tô de olho em você = I'm watching you, as a playful warning.
Dele is de + ele and means his. O nome dele = his name. Portuguese puts the owner after the noun.
